summary: Razorpay LIVE keys wiring verified end-to-end without ever completing a real payment. 13/13 backend pytest cases passed (pricing gateway routing, live order creation with correct paise amounts, DB persistence, bogus-signature rejection on /verify and /webhook, Stripe INTL regression, and professional-services scope guard). Frontend /pricing check found a CRITICAL name-shadowing bug that broke the entire Razorpay CTA flow — fixed and re-verified: modal now opens with LIVE Razorpay checkout (₹499, UPI/Cards/Netbanking, 'Secured by Razorpay') and was dismissed without paying.

ui_bugs.issue: Local `const startCheckout` shadowed the imported `startCheckout` from @/lib/checkout, causing infinite recursion on any CTA click. Result: 0 calls to /api/payments/razorpay/order, 0 loads of checkout.razorpay.com/v1/checkout.js, and ~80+ malformed /api/pricing/track POSTs returning 422 (plan field became an object). Razorpay modal never opened. Fix (applied by test agent): renamed local wrapper to `handleCheckout` and updated the onClick handler.

action_items: Review the Pricing.jsx rename fix (`startCheckout` -> `handleCheckout`) applied by the test agent to unblock the Razorpay CTA. Consider adding an ESLint rule (no-shadow) to catch this class of bug going forward.
Optional: reduce the /api/pricing/track spam risk by adding a client-side guard against duplicate/bad-shape event payloads.
critical_code_review_comments: Pricing.jsx defined `const startCheckout` inside the component with the exact same name as the imported helper — silent shadowing led to infinite recursion. This is a footgun; enable eslint `no-shadow` / `no-shadow-restricted-names` and prefer distinct handler names (e.g. handleCheckout).

monetize.py razorpay_create_order and razorpay_verify correctly re-derive amount/order_id from server-side sources (never the browser) — good. Signature check uses DB order_id, not the client value, which prevents client tampering.

razorpay_webhook returns 200 when RAZORPAY_KEY_ID or RAZORPAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET are unset; acceptable since keys ARE set in production, but consider hard-failing 503 to avoid silently accepting webhooks if a secret is ever unset.
services.py static-verified to contain zero razorpay references — professional-services scope guard is correct.
Minor: the review request refers to POST /api/services/request but the actual route is POST /api/service-request (submit_service_request). Not a bug, just a doc inconsistency.
test_credentials: Guest checkout only, X-Trade-Session: qa-rzp-iter40. No admin/login required. LIVE Razorpay keys were used ONLY for unpaid order creation and bogus-signature rejection paths (no real charges).
seed_data_creation: Created ~3 unpaid Razorpay orders and 1 Stripe INTL order in payment_transactions (all status=initiated, no charges). Test lead cleaned up in tearDown.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend Razorpay wiring is production-ready: /payments/pricing gateway routing, /payments/razorpay/order (paise = INR*100), /payments/razorpay/verify (rejects bogus signatures with 400, unknown order 404), /webhook/razorpay (rejects bad X-Razorpay-Signature with 400), Stripe INTL fallback intact, services module has no razorpay coupling. Frontend Pricing page CTA was fixed by renaming shadowed startCheckout to handleCheckout — CommandCenter.jsx and AccountPage.jsx do NOT have this bug (they invoke the imported startCheckout directly).
rca of the issue: In /app/frontend/src/pages/Pricing.jsx, `import { startCheckout } from '@/lib/checkout'` was shadowed by a component-local `const startCheckout = async (planKey) => {...}` that internally called `startCheckout({kind: planKey, ...})`. JavaScript resolved the inner call to the local function itself, not the imported one, producing infinite recursion. Symptoms observed: ~80 /pricing/track POSTs returning 422 within a couple seconds after any CTA click, and zero /payments/razorpay/order or checkout.js network activity. Fix: rename the local wrapper to `handleCheckout` and update onClick. After fix, verified single /razorpay/order request, single checkout.js load, and Razorpay modal opened with LIVE ₹499 payment options — modal dismissed without paying per safety instructions.
